get.summary:
An object's data, as a file to save. It's always sent as an attachment of
no particular type, so that a browser never renders it as part of the UI.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: The version to download; the current one if not given.

get.summary:
A bucket's lifecycle rules, as S3's GetBucketLifecycleConfiguration
gives them, but in the form they're stored in.

put.summary:
Replaces a bucket's lifecycle rules, as S3's
PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration does, which starts a new sweep of them.
Rules without an ID get one.

delete.summary:
Removes a bucket's lifecycle rules, as S3's DeleteBucketLifecycle does:
nothing expires from then on.

parameters.name: deleted
parameters.description: Also list keys whose current version is a delete marker.

get.summary: The nodes, each with the metrics it reports, if it's live.

post.summary:
Logs in to the KMS as each role without an identity there yet, from this
node, now rather than at its next maintenance pass. Fails with what went
wrong.

204.description: Every role has its identity in the KMS

get.summary:
How lifecycle sweeps are going: the rate, how long a round takes at it,
and each bucket's sweep.

post.summary:
Keeps a node that's being removed, or was, as `cairn node keep` does: it
gets shards again; those that moved stay where they are.

Starts removing a node, as `cairn node remove` does: it gets no new
shards, and its shards move to the other nodes (see `mover`).

put.summary: Makes a role an admin, or not.

post.summary: Grants permissions on an existing bucket.

parameters.name: permission
parameters.description: The permission to revoke; all of them on the bucket if not given.

put.summary:
Sets one of the redundancy settings (`data-shards`, `parity-shards`,
`repair-after`), for the whole cluster, as `cairn config set` does. The
node answering goes by it right away, the others within a heartbeat.

compact.description: Blobs with enough garbage to be compacted.

consolidate.description: Blobs small enough to be consolidated.

convert.description:
Replicated blobs old and large enough to be erasure-coded, once
coding is on (see `packer::coding`).

garbage_log.description:
Entries of the garbage log the packer hasn't folded yet: one per blob
that a statement deleted parts from.

moves.description:
Shards to move off nodes being removed, or down for longer than the
`repair-after` setting (see `mover`); and that setting, in minutes (0:
off).

packing.description: Blobs leased by packing jobs, right now.

garbage_bytes.description: Bytes of packed blobs that no part references anymore.

BucketLifecycle.description: A bucket's lifecycle rules, if it has any.

default_kms_key.description:
The KMS key of its default encryption (SSE-KMS), if it has one: what a
write that asks for no encryption of its own is encrypted with.

objects.description: Current versions that aren't delete markers.

roles.description: Roles with a grant on the bucket.

state.description:
`active`, `removing` (its shards are moving to other nodes, see
`mover`) or `removed`.

oneOf.description: What the node reported, if it's live and answered.

stats_error.description: Why a live node's stats are missing.

Counts.description: Counts of requests, by how they ended, and of what they moved.

client_errors.description: Answered with a 4xx: the client's fault (including denied requests).

latency_us.description: The sum of the times until the response's head was ready.

server_errors.description: Answered with a 5xx: a fault, or too few nodes.

Coverage.description: How much of the data the scrubber has checked (see `scrub`).

legacy_blobs.description: Committed blobs from before checksums, which can't be checked.

nodes.description:
What each node holds of checksummed data, and how recently it was
checked.

EncryptionInfo.description: How an object version is encrypted (see `s3::sse`).

kind.description:
`SSE-C` (with its client's key, which Cairn doesn't have), `SSE-KMS`
or `SSE-S3` (with Cairn's own key from the KMS).

kms_context.description: SSE-KMS: the encryption context its client gave, as JSON.

kms_key_id.description: SSE-KMS and SSE-S3: the name of the KMS key.

kms_key_version.description: SSE-KMS and SSE-S3: the version of the KMS key its data key is from.

oneOf.description: A "directory": the keys whose names continue past the prefix with `/`.

lost.description: Whether some of its bytes are intact on no replica (see `scrub`).

error.description: What went wrong, for a person to read.

bad_blocks.description: How many blocks failed; none if the whole file is at fault.

outcome.description:
`repaired`, `lost` (intact on no replica; still open), or `gone` (the
blob was deleted); none while open.

problem.description:
`missing`, `damaged`, or `catalog` (every block intact, but not the
file's CRC).

GcTotals.description: What garbage collection deleted since the node started.

Integrity.description:
What the scrubber found (see `scrub`): damaged and missing copies, and the
objects with data that's intact on no replica.

findings.description:
The open findings, then those resolved in the last 30 days, newest
first, up to 200.

lost.description:
The object versions (and uploads' parts) with lost bytes, the most
recently lost first, up to 500.

lost_objects.description: How many there are, all told.

recent.description:
Findings of the last day, by node: many of them in a short time are a
sign of a failing disk.

KmsLogin.description: A login to the KMS as a role.

at.description: When, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

error.description: Why it failed, if it did: what's likely wrong with the KMS's setup.

role.description: The role's ID, or `cairn` for Cairn itself (for SSE-S3).

KmsStatus.description: A node's KMS, as it sees it.

auth_mount.description:
Where the KMS's JWT auth method for Cairn is mounted (under `auth/`),
and the role of it that Cairn's logins use.

cairn_entity.description:
Cairn's own identity (entity) in the KMS, which is to be granted that
key, once the node has logged in as itself.

oneOf.description: The node's last login as a role, if it made one since it started.

last_success.description: When its last login that worked was, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

public_key.description:
The public key of the key the node signs its logins with (PEM): what
that auth method is to trust (`jwt_validation_pubkeys`). The same on
every node.

reachable.description: Whether the node could reach the KMS just now, and how it is.

sse_s3_key.description: SSE-S3's key, if Cairn has one: it uses it as itself.

LastSweep.description:
A bucket's last whole sweep, as `lifecycle_sweeps.last` keeps it. Times
are seconds since the Unix epoch.

last_step.description: When the last step began, and whether one is running now.

rate.description:
Object versions sweeps may read per hour, across the cluster; 0 if
they're paused.

reached_rate.description:
The rate steps have actually reached when they had more to do than
their share (an average over about the last hour), if they have.
Below `rate` if a step at a time can't go faster.

round_partial.description:
Whether some bucket has had no whole sweep yet, so that a round reads
more than `round_versions`.

round_secs.description:
How long a round takes at the rate reached, or set if it's lower (or
none was measured yet), in seconds; none if paused. Over a day, sweeps
fall behind, and expirations come that much later.

round_versions.description:
Versions a round of every bucket's sweep reads: the last whole sweep
of each, or what its first has read so far.

LifecycleBucket.description: A bucket's rules, and its sweep of them.

due.description:
When it gets its next turn: its next sweep, or, during one, its next
step (it's due if that's past).

rules.description: How many rules it has, and how many of them are enabled.

LifecycleDay.description: A day, UTC, as the number of days since 1970-01-01.

LifecycleFilter.description:
Which objects a rule applies to: those with keys starting with `prefix`,
and sizes strictly between the bounds. All of them, by default.

newer_versions.description: How many of the newest noncurrent versions are kept regardless.

enabled.description: `Status`: a disabled rule is kept, but does nothing.

id.description: Its name, unique among the bucket's rules; one is made up if empty.

Listing.description: A page of a bucket's keys, rolled up at `/` like a directory listing.

next.description: What to pass as `after` for the next page, if there is one.

lost_bytes.description: How many of its stored bytes are lost.

since.description: When the first of them was found lost.

version_id.description: The version; none for a part of an upload in progress.

events.description: The most recent things a pass did or failed at, oldest first.

last_duration.description: How many seconds the last pass took.

running_since.description: When the pass that's running started.

sweep_shard.description:
Where the GC's file sweep is, of `shards` (blob directories; the
names are the dashboard's).

MetricsReport.description: A node's metrics. Times are seconds since the Unix epoch.

in_flight.description: Requests whose response hasn't been sent in full yet.

rate.description: Object versions per hour, across the cluster; 0 pauses sweeps.

secret.description: At least 8 characters; one is generated if not given.
At least 8 characters; one is generated if not given.

NewSetting.description:
Sets the rate lifecycle sweeps go at, for the whole cluster.
A cluster setting's new value; `null` unsets it (it's back to its
default, or for `parity-shards`, every node goes by its flag again).

NodeCoverage.description:
The copies of committed, checksummed blobs a node holds, and how recently
they were known intact.

oldest_checked.description: When the least recently checked of the others was known intact.

unchecked.description:
Copies never checked (from before scrubbing), or flagged by a read:
checked next.

NodeHolding.description:
The committed blobs a node holds a shard of, and the bytes of those
shards.

shards.description: The shards it holds, which move to other nodes.

oneOf.description: The filesystem of its data dir, if it could tell.
Its KMS, if it has one (see `kms`).

now.description: The node's clock, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

scrub_rate.description: How many bytes per second its scrubber reads; 0 if it's off.

NodeStats.description:
What a node reports about itself, for the dashboard of any node (see
`peer`'s `/stats`).

ObjectInfo.description:
Every version of a key (the newest 200), each with its parts and where their
blobs are stored.

versions.description: Newest first; empty if there's no such key.

coding.description: Whether it's coded now: also takes as many live nodes as shards.

data_shards.description:
What cold data is erasure-coded into (the `data-shards` setting, and
the parity shards that `--replication-factor` gives), and how old it
must be. One data shard: it isn't.

max_data_shards.description: The most data and parity shards the settings allow.

parity_setting.description:
The `parity-shards` setting, if it's set; else every node goes by its
`--replication-factor`.

PackerTotals.description: What the packer did since the node started.

blob_offset.description: Where in the blob the part's bytes start.

crc64nvme.description: The CRC64/NVME of the part's bytes, in hex; none for old data.

data_shards.description:
The blob's data shards: 1 if it's replicated, else it's erasure-coded,
and readable with as many live shards.

lost.description:
The byte ranges of the part (as stored) that are intact on no
replica, as [start, stop) from its start (see `scrub`).

nodes.description: The nodes holding a shard of the blob.

Permission.description: A bucket-level permission a role can be granted.

ReplicaGroup.description:
The committed blobs of `data_shards` data shards (1: replicated) with
`copies` shards in all, `live` of them on live nodes. A blob is readable
with `data_shards` live shards, and as redundant as the cluster's
replication factor asks with `data_shards` + replication factor − 1.

history.description: The last hour's slots that had requests, oldest first.

ops.description: Since the node started, by operation.

slot_secs.description: How many seconds a slot of `history` covers.

RoleSummary.description: A role, never with its secret.

id.description:
Its ID, which never changes or comes back: its name (alias) in the
KMS's auth mount for Cairn.

kms_entity_id.description:
Its identity (entity) in the KMS, which key owners grant keys to;
none until Cairn has logged in as it, or without a KMS.

ScrubTotals.description:
What the scrubber did since the node started: the copies it checked (and
their bytes), how many of them it found damaged or missing, how many of
those it repaired, and how many have data that's intact nowhere, and how
many of its passes failed.

Secret.description: A role's secret, which is shown only this once.

warnings.description:
What's wrong with the cluster's layouts now, if anything: too few
nodes for them, say.

t.description: When the slot starts. The same on every node, so slots add up.

Storage.description:
What's stored where, how well it's replicated, and what the background jobs
still have to do.

key.description: The key it has got to.

oneOf.description: How it's encrypted; none if it isn't.

lost_bytes.description: How many of its parts' bytes are intact on no replica.

Versioning.description:
A bucket's versioning state. A bucket starts out unversioned; once enabled,
it only moves between enabled and suspended. Serialized as it's stored.
